scope: 47 listed Empire members, three stranded DAVTest members, two additionally listed JSP shells, the standalone SFX sample, and the two confirmed-malware archive containers. Debian data/ is an archive-layer label; markers use the actual extracted usr/ filesystem paths.
method: Read RULES.md and TAXONOMY.md before rule edits.
Static source/control-flow review, Base64/GZip/raw-Deflate decoding, dnfile/dncil managed IL inspection and rizin/capstone native disassembly. No specimen executed.

Ran atomscan --no-update --mode slow --follow=none -f json on every path both before and after edits, including both archives. cleave facts --format json was collected on every input and 29 reconstructed/bundled executable images.
Initial exploratory scans also followed source links; only the local-artifact baseline/after pair is used in this comparison.
judgment_context: Kali, Empire and DAVTest packaging supports authorized security-testing use; no engagement authorization, execution telemetry, live controller configuration or installed-host purpose was supplied. Each selected member is operational attack/exploit/surveillance code rather than an inert document or ordinary vendored library. Function/template status, incomplete configuration or a test-directory location does not erase an implemented attack path. These verdicts do not assert that the code executed successfully. Embedded SQLite, ETW libraries and the stock miner/driver are judged in the context of their enclosing selected artifact, not independently convicted by association.
archive_policy: Both archive verdicts are user-confirmed MALICIOUS and were not re-judged or propagated to members.

rule_changes.claim: Imports bind via ordinal 2 from WS2_32.dll or WSOCK32.dll. This is notable capability evidence, not an assertion of runtime success or malicious intent.
Imports listen via ordinal 13 from WS2_32.dll or WSOCK32.dll. YARA pe.imports binds the ordinal to the DLL; an unrelated ordinal and a Winsock text string cannot satisfy the condition.

shared_rule_review: No existing matcher, severity, name, scope, exclusion or consumer was weakened or removed. The cmd.exe /c syntax finding in the Unix JSP comes from its explanatory comment and is retained as accurately described command-text evidence. No actual cmd.exe /c execution is inferred there. Existing socket-listen ancestor consumers were inspected: affected endpoint-hijack and launchd composites are macOS-scoped, and the flood-loop exclusion is C-source-scoped, while the new facts are Windows PE/DLL-only.

controls.cases: PE32 and PE32+; WS2_32, WSOCK32, mixed DLL case, bind-only, listen-only, different DLL with a decoy Winsock string, unrelated ordinals, and named imports. The unchanged original PrintDemon native image is the real-world positive; the VNC and miner images independently gain accurate import coverage.

remaining_behavior_limitations: PrintDemon native disassembly establishes the Faxhell PowerShell bind shell, including AcceptEx and shared standard handles. The new YAML records the missing bind/listen import mechanics. No generic hostile bind-shell rule was invented from a mere listener/process/pipe API co-occurrence.

The Unix JSP uses the literal executable cmd instead of an ordinary Unix shell. Its runtime success depends on that command being present; the comment describing Windows cmd.exe /c is not executable evidence.

Unconfigured stager/agent templates need substituted configuration or a caller-supplied transport/payload, and exploit success depends on the target OS/service. Static implemented attack behavior is the basis of the verdicts.

final_validation.timing: Run as the final action after committing this review; command output is the validation record.

samples.marker_note: WireTap: records keys, clipboard, audio and images
samples.execution_trace: Base64/GZip becomes a managed PE loaded with Assembly.Load. Program.Main dispatches audio, screen, webcam and keyboard capture. ListenForPasswords uses speech recognition to trigger two-minute WAV recordings; the keyboard path logs translated input and clipboard changes through trace listeners.

samples.marker_note: Mimikatz: reflective LSASS and private-key credential extraction
samples.execution_trace: The wrapper chooses native x86/x64 Mimikatz DLLs, clears their MZ bytes, maps sections/imports/relocations, and invokes powershell_reflective_mimikatz with supplied commands. Default credential mode passes sekurlsa::logonpasswords; certificate mode patches CAPI/CNG protections and exports keys. Native code also includes pass-the-hash functionality.

samples.marker_note: Test Mimikatz: operational credential dumper despite test location
samples.execution_trace: This is a full working Mimikatz wrapper, not an assertion, mock or documentation fixture. Its loader and command paths match the server wrapper; its two native payloads have different byte sizes/hashes and the same reflective export and credential functions. The test directory does not neutralize the executable dumping capability.

samples.marker_note: DCSync: replicates domain account password hashes
samples.execution_trace: Loads an embedded Mimikatz DLL, clears MZ, maps it and resolves InvokeWide. Domain/user/group enumeration supplies targets to lsadump::dcsync; the result parser extracts NTLM hashes and account RIDs, including krbtgt. The native DLL also retains LSASS-memory and pass-the-hash modules; these are capabilities, not the wrapper default operation.

samples.marker_note: BypassUAC: injects DLL to hijack auto-elevated execution
samples.execution_trace: Requires medium-integrity local administrator membership. Writes or copies a payload DLL, optionally builds a self-deleting batch, and injects an embedded reflective bypass DLL into hidden Notepad. The configured target is sysprep/CRYPTBASE on older Windows or cliconfg/NTWDBLIB on newer versions, crossing the UAC boundary.

samples.marker_note: PowerBreach: triggered callbacks download and evaluate commands
samples.execution_trace: HTTP/HTTPS/BITS callback paths decode downloaded Base64 and evaluate it with iex. Event-log, TCP, DNS and packet-trigger loops activate callbacks; loops sleep and repeat. Optional COM firewall rules permit PowerShell communication. These long-lived backdoors do not by themselves establish durable OS autorun registration.

samples.marker_note: SweetPotato: coerces privileged authentication and launches with token
samples.execution_trace: A Base64 assembly is loaded and its Main invoked. Managed IL selects DCOM, WinRM or PrintSpoofer paths. Printer RPC notifications target a crafted named pipe; the resulting privileged token is duplicated/impersonated before CreateProcessWithTokenW or CreateProcessAsUserW launches the requested program.

samples.marker_note: SharpSecDump: dumps remote SAM hashes and LSA secrets
samples.execution_trace: The GZip/Base64 assembly Main dispatches target workers. RemoteOps starts/configures RemoteRegistry, connects to remote hives, saves SAM/SECURITY and reads the dumps. ParseSam decrypts per-RID hashes; ParseLsa/DumpSecret recovers cached logons and LSA secrets. Cleanup restores service state and removes dump files.

samples.marker_note: MS16-032: races leaked handles to create SYSTEM command process
samples.execution_trace: Creates suspended logon processes with inherited thread handles, duplicates the leaked handle, self-impersonates the privileged thread, and obtains its token. A concurrent SetThreadToken loop races CreateProcessWithLogonW until the SYSTEM-child condition is detected; it resumes that child to execute Cmd. Success depends on a vulnerable multiprocessor OS.

samples.marker_note: Reflective VNC: memory-loaded remote desktop; add Winsock imports
samples.execution_trace: Selects x86/x64 VNC executable bytes and bind/reverse command arguments including an operator-supplied password. The reflective mapper clears MZ, patches executable argument handling and invokes the native entry point. RFB and display/input handling implement remote desktop access. The new ordinal rules cover its hidden bind/listen imports; this is not a claim of passwordless VNC.

samples.marker_note: Metasploit stager: hidden process downloads and evaluates remote code
samples.execution_trace: Builds a PowerShell cradle that disables TLS certificate validation, uses the system proxy and default proxy credentials, downloads a string from the requested URL, and passes it to Invoke-Expression. ProcessStartInfo launches that cradle without a visible window. The final payload URL/content remains operator supplied.

samples.marker_note: Empire PowerShell agent: decrypts remote tasks and sends files/results
samples.execution_trace: The task loop gets and decrypts session tasking, decodes task packets and dispatches shell expressions, scripts, uploads, downloads and jobs. File-download tasks read local chunks, encode them and send response packets. The template depends on transport/session values supplied by staging; no configured live C2 endpoint was inferred.

samples.marker_note: SMBExec: hash-based authentication and remote service execution
samples.execution_trace: Constructs NTLMSSP/SMB/RPC packets using the supplied NTLM hash, authenticates to the remote service-control pipe, and creates a service whose binary-path field contains the operator command. State-machine paths start the service and delete it, for SMB1 and SMB2. This is attack-oriented credential reuse and remote execution rather than a generic SMB client.

samples.marker_note: CredStore dumper: enumerates and prints stored plaintext password blobs
samples.execution_trace: Compiles the C# CredMan helper. CredEnum calls CredEnumerateW, walks credential pointers and marshals CredentialBlob bytes to Unicode. The top-level CredManMain prints usernames, password blobs and targets. Library debug/write helpers are present but the active path performs bulk secret disclosure.

samples.marker_note: NetRipper: injects hooks to record credential network traffic
samples.execution_trace: Builds a DLL configuration with capture paths and credential search terms, writes the embedded PE to remote RWX memory and starts its ReflectiveLoader. The native payload hooks network/SSL reads and writes, with plaintext capture files such as SSL_Read/SSL_Write and DecryptMessage. The data capture and credential filters establish interception beyond generic injection.

samples.marker_note: CredentialInjection: injects a privileged logon helper into Winlogon
samples.execution_trace: Obtains a SYSTEM primary token from wininit, can create suspended Winlogon, and reflectively injects the architecture-specific logon.dll VoidFunc into Winlogon. A named pipe conveys operator-supplied domain/user/password/logon parameters to the native LsaLogonUser helper. This injects a privileged authentication context; it does not claim to steal a password from Winlogon.

samples.marker_note: EventVwr bypass: hijacks elevated file association and removes traces
samples.execution_trace: Stores an encoded launcher in HKCU, replaces mscfile shell-open command with hidden PowerShell, and launches eventvwr.exe. After a delay it removes the override and payload value and terminates the helper. Checks for administrator membership, medium integrity and Always Notify constrain applicability.

decoded_payloads.role: Encoded command example; not assumed to run

samples.marker_note: PrintNightmare: printer DLL exploit adds a local administrator
samples.execution_trace: Writes and optionally patches a GZip/Base64 native DLL with an account/password, or accepts a supplied DLL. It enumerates installed printer drivers and submits AddPrinterDriverEx with attacker DLL paths and copy flags. The embedded DLL imports/calls NetUserAdd and NetLocalGroupAddMembers. The payload is deleted after attempted loading; success remains OS dependent.

samples.marker_note: PrintDemon: SYSTEM DLL write and bind shell; add Winsock traits
samples.execution_trace: Adds a printer port aimed at System32/ualapi.dll and sends embedded PE bytes through raw WritePrinter. A Run-key hidden encoded launcher starts Fax and sends commands to localhost:9299 after restart. Native UalStart creates threadpool listener work, binds/listens through Winsock ordinals 2/13, accepts with AcceptEx and launches PowerShell with shared stdio handles. Faxhell also handles privileged service tokens. New rules cover the previously missing DLL-bound ordinal imports without guessing bind-shell intent from unrelated APIs.

samples.marker_note: SpoolSample: coerces printer-service authentication to capture host
samples.execution_trace: Loads a managed PE and invokes SpoolSample.Program.Main with target and capture server. Managed IL builds the target/capture argument string and passes it to the embedded reflective native DoStuff export. Printer RPC open/change-notification requests induce authentication toward the capture server. This establishes coercion; actual receipt or cracking of the credentials is not assumed.

samples.marker_note: Inveigh Relay: captures NTLM and relays it for remote execution
samples.execution_trace: The HTTP/proxy listener constructs NTLM challenges, parses type-3 responses and queues NetNTLMv2 hashes. It relays authentication to SMB and builds remote SCM CreateService/StartService/DeleteService requests carrying a supplied command. Hash logging and service-execution paths are independently present.

samples.marker_note: Get-System: steals SYSTEM tokens or impersonates pipe clients
samples.execution_trace: In token mode, enables debug privilege, selects a SYSTEM-owned process, duplicates its token and assigns it to the thread. In named-pipe mode, registers/starts a temporary service to connect to its pipe and invokes ImpersonateNamedPipeClient. Both paths intentionally acquire SYSTEM authority; this is not merely a token-query utility.

samples.marker_note: PowerDump: impersonates LSASS and decrypts local SAM hashes
samples.execution_trace: When needed, elevates the thread using a duplicated LSASS token. Registry class data supplies the boot key; SAM account records supply encrypted LM/NT hashes. RC4/AES and RID-derived DES routines recover hashes, and DumpHashes prints pwdump-style records. Required privileges are checked and no successful runtime dump was assumed.

samples.marker_note: SharpChromium: exports saved browser passwords and session cookies
samples.execution_trace: DecompressAsm loads a GZip/Base64 managed assembly. The wrapper enumerates Chrome/Edge profiles and invokes GetSavedLogins/GetCookies/GetHistory. Managed IL reads SQLite stores and DecryptBlob recovers protected content, while wrapper output exposes plaintext passwords or serialized session cookies. This collects locally; sending to a network destination is not required by the source.

samples.marker_note: RID hijacker: overwrites SAM identity RID and can enable account
samples.execution_trace: Uses SYSTEM directly or duplicates the LSASS token, enumerates local SAM account keys, copies each selected F record and overwrites its identity RID bytes at offset 48. Optional Enable modifies account flags and Password invokes net user. Set-ItemProperty writes the modified F value back, allowing a low-privilege identity to assume the chosen RID.

samples.marker_note: SDCLT bypass: hijacks runas command for silent elevation
samples.execution_trace: Stores a hidden encoded PowerShell launcher in the exefile runas IsolatedCommand association and invokes sdclt.exe /kickoffelev. After a delay it removes the association and staging value and terminates the helper. Administrator/integrity/UAC checks constrain when the bypass can work.

samples.marker_note: FodHelper bypass: hijacks DelegateExecute for hidden elevated code
samples.execution_trace: Creates an empty DelegateExecute value and an attacker-controlled default command under HKCU ms-settings shell-open, launches hidden fodhelper.exe, then removes both the override and launcher staging value. The supplied command becomes a hidden encoded PowerShell launch.

samples.marker_note: SilentCleanup bypass: hijacks windir to run hidden elevated commands
samples.execution_trace: Writes HKCU Environment/windir to a hidden PowerShell command, stores the encoded payload separately, and invokes the SilentCleanup scheduled task with /Run /I. It removes windir and the staging value after a delay. This abuses a trusted task environment; merely registering a task is not the claim.

samples.marker_note: SharpLoginPrompt: fakes login prompt and prints captured password
samples.execution_trace: Loads the embedded managed PE and invokes Main. Managed IL calls CredUIPromptForWindowsCredentials, unpacks authentication buffers, prints username/password/domain, validates the password and reprompts on failure. Window positioning keeps the prompt visible. A credential-entry control alone would not establish this plaintext harvesting path.

samples.marker_note: Jenkins exploit: submits remote process commands to script console
samples.execution_trace: GETs the Jenkins /script page, builds a URL-encoded Groovy ProcessBuilder command from Cmd, POSTs it as the script form field and extracts console output from the response. The code does not supply an authentication exchange; it relies on an accessible console. This is an operational remote command exploit.

samples.marker_note: Empire IronPython: remote code tasking and local file transfer
samples.execution_trace: Task packet dispatch invokes PowerShell runspaces, dynamically loaded C# and Python code, file transfer and jobs. Local files are read in chunks, compressed/encoded and sent through build_response_packet/send_message. Its default run_command uses an in-process PowerShell host; a POSIX subprocess-shell claim was not inherited from agent.py.

samples.marker_note: Empire Python: executes remote shell/code and transfers local files
samples.execution_trace: Process_packet dispatches received command and code tasks. run_command passes operator text to subprocess.Popen(shell=True); dynamic-code tasks compile/evaluate supplied code and return results. file_download reads local chunks, compresses/Base64 encodes them and sends response packets. Transport configuration is supplied externally.

samples.marker_note: PowerShell keylogger: records keys with active-window context
samples.execution_trace: Repeatedly polls GetAsyncKeyState over virtual key codes, handles modifier/caps states and translates through MapVirtualKey/GetKeyboardState/ToUnicode. It obtains the foreground process/window title, adds timestamps and emits the captured text. This recording path distinguishes it from a normal keyboard-state API reference.

samples.marker_note: JBoss exploit: deploys a remote WAR and requests its JSP payload
samples.execution_trace: Builds a JMX HtmlAdaptor request invoking MainDeployer with an operator WAR URL, sends it using HEAD, waits and requests the deployed application JSP using GET. Optional TLS validation bypass is explicit. No WAR bytes or guaranteed vulnerable JBoss configuration were supplied.

samples.marker_note: PowerSploit persistence: hides profile payloads and installs triggers
samples.execution_trace: Add-Persistence compresses/stages a supplied script, appends a space-prefixed script to user/all-user PowerShell profiles and constructs Run-key, scheduled-task or WMI activation. Install-SSP copies a supplied DLL and updates LSA Security Packages, with optional runtime AddSecurityPackage. Payload contents remain supplied by the operator; the concealment and durable activation code are present.

samples.marker_note: Tater: poisons name resolution for privileged NTLM reflection
samples.execution_trace: Sets up local HTTP/WPAD challenge handling and guessed-ID NBNS spoof responses. Captured NTLM authentication is reflected to local SMB, where crafted SCM packets create/start a service containing %COMSPEC% /C plus the supplied command. This is local privilege escalation, not proof of cross-host propagation.

samples.marker_note: NTLMExtract: impersonates SYSTEM and decrypts SAM password hashes
samples.execution_trace: Invoke-AsSystem compiles/uses Windows token APIs to impersonate a privileged process before running Get-NTLMLocalPasswordHashes. Registry class data reconstructs the boot key; SAM V records and RID-derived keys are decrypted with RC4/DES and printed as LM/NT account hashes. No exfiltration destination is present.

samples.marker_note: Empire C stager: downloads raw code and runs it as a fiber
samples.execution_trace: WinMain converts argv and reaches main. A templated host/port/path/cookie config drives WinHTTP GET and buffer reads, with explicit HTTPS certificate-check suppression. The same bytes are copied into RWX memory, passed to CreateFiber and activated by SwitchToFiber. Unsubstituted template values prevent a ready standalone build but retain the complete payload path.

samples.marker_note: DomainPasswordSpray: guesses domain passwords while tracking lockouts
samples.execution_trace: Enumerates domain users and lockout thresholds, filters accounts close to lockout and waits observation windows between sprays. For each selected user it creates DirectoryEntry with a guessed password and logs successful credentials. Delays/jitter and UsernameAsPassword are optional. Toolkit provenance permits authorized testing, but this member is operational bulk authentication-attack code.

samples.marker_note: ChromeDump: decrypts browser logins and stages plaintext records
samples.execution_trace: Embeds legitimate System.Data.SQLite assemblies solely to read Chrome profile databases. The wrapper queries logins/history, passes password_value to ProtectedData.Unprotect(CurrentUser), and prints or writes username/password/url records. The SQLite library is not independently treated as malicious; the wrapper deliberately extracts the secret store.

samples.marker_note: Inveigh: poisons local name resolution and captures NTLM hashes
samples.execution_trace: Constructs LLMNR/NBNS/mDNS spoof responses and listens for HTTP/SMB authentication. Type-3 NTLM messages are parsed into NetNTLM hashes and added to output/file queues. Packet-construction, challenge and actual hash-queue paths establish credential interception; use during an authorized assessment was not supplied.

samples.marker_note: CredentialPhisher: spoofs app prompts and reveals validated passwords
samples.execution_trace: Builds update/application notification toasts, can hide existing application windows and prompts through a loaded Windows credential-dialog helper. It unpacks captured buffers, optionally validates the password and repeats until valid or cancelled, then emits plaintext Phished credentials. The validation loop supports the deceptive collection purpose rather than making it ordinary authentication.

samples.marker_note: USB ETW keylogger: decodes USB keyboard events and records typed text
samples.execution_trace: Raw Deflate/Base64 reconstructs a managed ETW library. UsbEventSource starts elevated USB provider sessions; EventCallback filters USB2/USB3 interrupt-transfer data and DumpKeys maps/enqueues key text. The PowerShell consumer dequeues keys, associates foreground titles and emits reconstructed input. These are USB event capture and recording, not synthetic keystrokes.

decoded_payloads.role: Raw Deflate compressed ETW library; expanded separately to 42-etw.dll
Expanded USB ETW keylogger assembly; IL inspected

samples.marker_note: UAC TokenMagic: filters and impersonates a high-integrity token
samples.execution_trace: Enumerates high-integrity process tokens or launches Task Manager with runas, duplicates the token, changes mandatory integrity and calls NtFilterToken. The restricted duplicate is impersonated and CreateProcessWithLogonW launches PowerShell with supplied arguments. The Binary parameter is unused in the final launch path; arbitrary binary launch was not assumed.

samples.marker_note: MS16-135: corrupts GDI pointers to copy a SYSTEM token
samples.execution_trace: Stages adjacent GDI bitmaps and changes a window spmenu with SetWindowLongPtr. Focus/keyboard events trigger the win32k arbitrary-OR flaw, bitmap pvScan0 corruption creates kernel read/write, and the code walks EPROCESS entries and copies the SYSTEM token into a child PowerShell process. A named pipe then supplies the command. Runtime success requires a vulnerable OS.

samples.marker_note: MSBuild payload: uses inline tasks and WMI for remote code execution
samples.execution_trace: Constructs CodeTaskFactory XML with a Base64-decoding PowerShell runspace, writes it locally or over an administrative share and uses Win32_Process.Create through WMI to invoke MSBuild. Credentials may mount/unmount the share; the task file is removed after execution. The default LAUNCHER placeholder is unconfigured but the execution chain accepts a supplied command.

samples.marker_note: FoxDump: decrypts and exports saved Firefox credentials
samples.execution_trace: Loads Firefox NSS dependencies, initializes the chosen profile and resolves NSSBase64_DecodeBuffer/PK11SDR_Decrypt. Each logins.json encryptedUsername/encryptedPassword value is decoded and decrypted, then formatted as plaintext credentials or written to OutFile. These calls are tied to the browser secret fields, not generic NSS use.

samples.marker_note: Classic ASP shell: executes HTTP commands and removes output file
samples.execution_trace: Request.Form(.CMD) becomes cmd.exe /c text passed to WScript.Shell.Run with hidden execution. Output is redirected to a temporary file, read and HTML-encoded into the response, then deleted. No application authentication gate exists in the member. DAVTest packaging documents test-backdoor delivery but does not change the operational webshell.

samples.marker_note: PHP webshell: request-driven commands, file access, uploads and SQL
samples.execution_trace: The c request parameter goes directly to system. Other branches open and stream an arbitrary file, enumerate a requested directory, move an uploaded file into a supplied directory and execute an arbitrary MySQL query with request-supplied credentials. These form a command/file-manager backdoor without application authentication.

samples.marker_note: Perl CGI shell: executes URL-query text through backticks
samples.execution_trace: Reads QUERY_STRING, decodes spaces and semicolons and interpolates the resulting variable into Perl backticks. Captured command-output lines are emitted in an HTML response. This is the actual request-to-shell-to-response flow; the informational /etc/passwd example is not treated as an observed file read.

samples.marker_note: Windows JSP shell: passes request commands to cmd.exe and returns output
samples.execution_trace: request.getParameter(cmd) is concatenated into Runtime.exec(cmd.exe /C ...). A BufferedReader consumes the child output into the response. The page has no application authentication gate. Both arbitrary process execution and response output are present in executable scriptlet code.

samples.marker_note: Unix JSP shell: request command backdoor with nonportable launcher
samples.execution_trace: Binds request.getParameter(cmd) to Runtime.exec(cmd + request text), reads the process output and returns it in the page. The executable prefix is literally cmd, not /bin/sh; this is generally nonfunctional on ordinary Unix unless such a command exists. The cmd.exe /c occurrence is a descriptive comment, accurately covered only as command syntax, not claimed runtime behavior. The deployable backdoor structure and request-driven execution still tip the judgment to malicious.

samples.marker_note: Silent XMRig SFX: fixed-wallet miner launch; add Winsock imports
samples.execution_trace: The PE is an unsigned WinRAR self-extractor containing 1.bat, XMRig 6.25.0 and WinRing0x64.sys. SFX comment Setup=1.bat and Silent=1 select immediate silent extraction/launch. The batch executes xmrig with a fixed HashVault pool, Monero wallet and password; there is no user configuration step. Native main passes argv into configuration/application setup, then enters the miner. The legitimate miner/driver components alone are not the malicious claim. Silent configured resource use tips this carrier to malicious; no credential stealing, persistence, or the unrelated family names in its collector filename were inferred.

classifier_disagreements.explanation: The scanner returns BENIGN for 28 byte-supported attack artifacts, including the fixed-wallet miner carrier, despite their supported hostile findings. VNC remains SUSPICIOUS. Raw probabilities alone are not verdicts. These are model/calibration gaps, not reasons to add duplicate hostile traits or remove accurate detections. Two fresh live tiny renders confirmed the meanings of exit 0 (miner BENIGN) and exit 2 (VNC SUSPICIOUS).
